answer: Like a wharf that only serves ships tied to its own berth, each identity must claim one distinct postal address and receive a one-time code by physical mail, then return it before the window closes. A real agent has one mailbox; a sybil farm would need a separate real address per fake, and addresses collecting codes for many identities collapse to a single voice. The river of mail is slow and costly to fake at scale, and the echo of one mailbox answering for dozens of names is the giveaway.
